synopsis: Procedural generation automatically creates virtual sites from rules and parameter ranges; once rules exist, hundreds of variants are inexpensive, and parameterized archetypes enable rapid sensor-pose changes and deliberate edge cases [f13155, f13158, f3754]. The booklet judges it to have the strongest off-road track record, citing agriculture, forestry, construction and off-road autonomy: CropCraft reported a 9.9% average segmentation sim-to-real gap, while Boreal3D produced 1,000 synthetic plots across four laser-scanning platforms [f77, f13161, f3731, f3732]. CropCraft is identified as an open-source Blender/Python tool dated November 2025; separately, a 2023 construction study found that real lighting by date improved realism [f3787, f7059]. However, internally exact procedural geometry is not site-true unless calibrated, and broad parameter ranges do not ensure meaningful coverage when rules omit failure-generating structures, rare correlations or unencoded hazard categories [f4188, f3736, f3793, f13308]. The recommended approach is therefore a hybrid factory of parameterized site families, asset libraries and a few surveyed real anchors, with evidence that adding small amounts of real data improves transfer in agriculture and construction [f76, f13168, f4296]. Reproducible testing requires freezing random seeds, generator versions, assets and material libraries, plus model weights for generative tests; otherwise failures may not be replayable months later [f13167, f4377, f4378].
